definition: A basic type of feedforward neural network consisting of multiple layers of neurons, each fully connected to the next, capable of modeling non-linear relationships.
details: MLPs are a foundational neural network architecture and remain common building blocks within more complex architectures, such as the feedforward sub-layers within transformer blocks.

explainer.lead: An MLP is a feedforward network of fully connected neuron layers that learns nonlinear mappings from input to output. It matters as a foundational building block reused inside larger architectures.

tiers.eli5: Layers of workers pass a message along, each one adjusting it slightly, until the last layer gives the answer.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers stack dense layers with nonlinear activations and train by backpropagation. A pitfall is that full connectivity inflates parameter counts and overfits small datasets without regularisation.
tiers.paperLevel: Each layer computes a weighted sum of the previous layer's outputs plus a bias, passed through a nonlinear activation: h = f(Wx + b), stacked over multiple layers. Limits: no inherent handling of sequence or spatial structure, and heavy parameter cost.

explainer.example: A two-layer MLP with 784 inputs, a hidden layer and 10 outputs classifies handwritten digit images by passing each 28x28 image through the weighted layers.
